You are ONE OF FOUR independent reviewers of a pull request. Work alone; do not assume another reviewer covers anything.

REPO: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa

=== ACCESS RULES (STRICT) ===
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, commit, push, or post anything to GitHub.
- DO NOT check out any branch. The working tree holds unrelated uncommitted work.
- PR fetched as local ref `pr/61`. Read with `git show pr/61:<path>`.
- Base (merge-base with develop) `8362b3c`. Read with `git show 8362b3c:<path>`.
- Diff with `git diff 8362b3c pr/61 [-- <path>]`.
- DO NOT re-run any gate. Gates were already measured; numbers below.

=== THE PR ===
#61 "SFCC-751: BrowserStack/Zephyr Scale QA automation pipeline", author TimLavelleACC,
`feature/browserstack-ci-automation` -> `develop`. 42 files, +2886/-266, 20 commits. Head 74e2b82.
CodeRabbit approved after several CHANGES_REQUESTED rounds; no human review yet.

=== JIRA TICKET SFCC-751 — VERBATIM, AS WRITTEN ===
Title: SFCC-751: QA Pipeline — Playwright spec generation, BrowserStack execution, and Zephyr Scale result sync

Overview
Implement the end-to-end QA pipeline that closes the loop between Zephyr Scale test cases and BrowserStack Automate execution results. This story covers three discrete deliverables that must be in place for the AI-assisted QA methodology to function as designed.

Background
Zephyr test case SFCC-T150 has been created and linked to SFCC-420. The pipeline requires:
- A Playwright spec tagged with the Zephyr test case key so BrowserStack knows what it is executing
- A GitHub Actions workflow that fetches BrowserStack results and posts execution records back to Zephyr Scale via the EU regional API
- A validated end-to-end run confirming the full chain works

Deliverables
Deliverable 1 — Playwright spec (SFCC-T150)
- Generate e2e/tests/zimm/integrations/SFCC-420-global-e-job-site-assignments.p1.spec.ts
- Spec must be tagged with Zephyr test case key SFCC-T150
- Scenarios must cover all 6 BDD scenarios in SFCC-T150
- Selectors via POM only — no inline selectors
- Tagged @SFCC-420 @global-e @integration @p1

Deliverable 2 — GitHub Actions sync script
- New workflow: .github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml
- Triggers on completion of BrowserStack Automate run in CI
- Fetches BrowserStack session results via BrowserStack REST API
- Maps BrowserStack pass/fail to Zephyr test case key via spec tag
- Posts execution record to Zephyr Scale EU endpoint: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2/testexecutions
- Attaches BrowserStack session URL and HAR to Zephyr execution record
- Zephyr API token stored as GitHub Actions secret: ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN
- BrowserStack credentials stored as: BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME, BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY

Deliverable 3 — End-to-end validation
- Trigger a BrowserStack run against the new spec
- Confirm execution record appears in Zephyr under SFCC-T150
- Confirm BrowserStack session URL is attached to the Zephyr execution record
- Document any manual steps required for ongoing operation

Acceptance Criteria
- Given a merged Playwright spec tagged with a Zephyr test case key, when BrowserStack Automate completes a run in CI, then an execution record is created in Zephyr Scale under the correct test case with pass/fail status and BrowserStack session URL attached
- Given the sync script runs, when it calls the Zephyr API, then it uses the EU regional endpoint https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 and not the US default
- Given a BrowserStack run fails, when the sync script posts to Zephyr, then the execution record status is Failed and the BrowserStack session URL for debugging is included
- Given the pipeline runs end-to-end, when reviewed in Zephyr Scale, then SFCC-T150 shows an execution record linked to the BrowserStack run with correct status

Design/Technical Notes
- Zephyr Scale instance is on EU/DE regional API: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2
- Do NOT use the US default endpoint https://api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 — returns unknown token errors
- BrowserStack Automate REST API
- Zephyr Scale test executions API: POST /testexecutions with testCaseKey, testCycleKey, statusName, comment
- The .browserstack.yml is already scoped to e2e/tests/zimm — new spec picked up automatically
- Playwright spec naming convention: {JIRA-KEY}-{description}.{priority}.spec.ts
=== END VERBATIM TICKET ===

=== ALREADY-MEASURED GATE RESULTS (do not re-run) ===
PR touches ZERO files under `overrides/`. Coverage of the 42 changed files: lint 0/42, audit:tokens 0/42 (exits 1 at healthy baseline, 14 known pre-existing; not in CI), tsc 1/42, Vitest 0/42 changed (PASSED only because detect-changes watches vitest.config.*), Storybook 0/42 changed, Playwright E2E localhost SKIPPING, BrowserStack E2E SKIPPING, Deploy Preview PASSED, File Tier & Squad Boundary PASSED.
A SKIPPED required check counts as PASSING on the merge button here. Do NOT read these as evidence about this PR.

=== ALREADY SETTLED BY THE LEAD — do not re-litigate ===
The `.browserstack.yml` -> `browserstack.yml` rename did NOT drop Tier 1 status (frozenFiles.md:114 + CODEOWNERS:60 at head cover it). Still fair game: `protected-file-guard.yml` has no browserstack entry at base OR head.

=== YOUR ANGLE: R4 — FAILURE MODES & SECURITY ===
Error handling, silent failures, fallbacks that mask bugs, fail-open behaviour, and security-sensitive paths. This PR introduces new network I/O, new secrets, and code that WRITES to external systems (Jira, Zephyr).

1. **`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` (new, 359 lines)** — the main target.
   - Enumerate EVERY `warn()`-and-continue path vs every `die()`-and-exit path. For each warn path, state what silently does not happen as a result, and whether a human would ever learn.
   - The script parses a BrowserStack `hierarchy[]` response shape. Its own comments reportedly admit this shape has NEVER been exercised against a real payload in this account. Treat that comment as a CLAIM: verify whether the code defends against a shape mismatch, or whether a mismatch yields a silent zero-result run that exits 0 and reports "nothing to sync".
   - `ZEPHYR_API_URL` -> `ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL` is derived by replacing a `/testcases` suffix with `/testexecutions`. What happens when the configured URL does NOT end in `/testcases`? Trace the resulting request target. Is it detectable, or does it POST executions to the wrong endpoint?
   - **It automatically CREATES Jira Bug issues, and auto-assigns them**, on failed tests. This is an outward-facing write to a real system. What bounds it? Is there any cap, dedupe, or dry-run? What happens on a run where many tests fail at once (e.g. an environment outage, or a bad RETAIL_APP_HOME causing every page load to fail)? Could it mass-create issues? Who gets assigned when the lookup falls back?
   - Does anything log a secret, a token, an Authorization header, or a full request/response body?
2. **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` (new)** — the relevance check reportedly defaults `relevant=true` when the artifact cannot be downloaded or read (`continue-on-error: true`). Verify. Fail-open onto a PAID BrowserStack run is a cost and a correctness issue — quantify what triggers it.
3. **`.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml` (new)** — new secret `GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN` used to read GitHub Environment variables, plus `MRT_USER`/`MRT_API_KEY`. What scope does this token need, and is it used safely? Does anything it fetches get echoed into logs, a PR comment, or an artifact? It upserts a PR comment — can any environment value leak into that comment?
4. **`workflow_run` trigger security.** `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` and `zephyr-results-sync.yml` both trigger on `workflow_run`. `workflow_run` executes in the context of the DEFAULT branch with access to secrets, even when the triggering run came from a fork or an untrusted branch. Assess: can an untrusted PR influence what these workflows execute, what they check out, or what they send to Jira/Zephyr/BrowserStack? Check what ref each checks out and whether any PR-controlled data reaches a shell command unquoted (script injection via `${{ }}` interpolation into `run:` blocks is the classic vector — grep for it).
5. **`.env.sample`** changes — per AGENTS.md, never put tokens/bearer creds/DSNs/licence keys there; keys must be tagged `# scope:...` on their own line above the key, and a blank placeholder must stay truly blank (the pre-commit secret guard reads a trailing-comment value as non-empty). Verify every added key.
6. **Credential handling in the new e2e page objects / fixtures** — `e2e/fixtures/products.js`, `sitePrefixes.js`, `e2e/support/pages/*.js`. Any hardcoded credential, real customer data, or environment-specific secret?

=== CONSTRAINTS ON YOUR OUTPUT (all mandatory) ===
- FALSIFY, do not confirm. Attack each claim the PR makes about itself — especially reassuring claims written in its own source comments. "CodeRabbit flagged this and it was fixed" is a claim, not evidence; verify the fix.
- Cite `file:line` for every finding.
- Label each finding CONFIRMED (proved) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned but unproven).
- Severity: BLOCKER, DEFECT, or NOTE.
- When a count moves, prove WHICH items moved, not just how many.
- For any check whose pass you rely on, try to make it pass WRONGLY — construct a decoy that should fail and reason whether it would.
- Any "X exists nowhere" claim MUST state its search scope in the same sentence (e.g. "no `${{ github.event` interpolation inside a `run:` block anywhere in .github/workflows/ at pr/61").
- Separate author-introduced from pre-existing. Pre-existing -> NOTE unless the PR's own premise makes it a defect.
- MANDATORY CLOSING SECTION "What I could not verify": name what you could not reach and why; show the search if you believe the space is covered. An empty section with no reasoning is a failed brief.

Be concrete and concise. No long code dumps.

1	name: Zephyr Results Sync
     2	
     3	# SFCC-751 Deliverable 2. Runs after every completed run of either workflow
     4	# that can produce a BrowserStack build — QA (release/** PRs,
     5	# e2e-browserstack) or Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)
     6	# (develop-PR path, e2e-browserstack-preview.yml, split out 2026-08-25 to
     7	# stop polling for Deploy Preview — see that workflow's own comment) — and
     8	# syncs any BrowserStack Test Observability results tagged @zephyr:<KEY>
     9	# to Zephyr Scale (DE-hosted — BrowserStack's native Zephyr integration
    10	# can't reach it, see scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs's doc comment and
    11	# .docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md). On a failing test it also
    12	# files a Jira defect with evidence, since BrowserStack's own "Report a
    13	# bug" flow is manual-UI-only — confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for
    14	# automatic-on-failure filing.
    15	on:
    16	  workflow_run:
    17	    workflows: ['QA', 'Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)']
    18	    types: [completed]
    19	
    20	permissions:
    21	  contents: read
    22	  actions: read # to download the build-name artifact from the triggering run
    23	
    24	jobs:
    25	  sync:
    26	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    27	    # Skip only a fully cancelled run — a triggering run that failed
    28	    # elsewhere (e.g. unit-tests, or the develop-PR path's own PR/Jira-key
    29	    # lookup) may still have a real BrowserStack build worth syncing. The
    30	    # sync script itself no-ops cleanly if no build exists for this run
    31	    # (e2e-browserstack is conditionally gated on both workflows, so most
    32	    # runs won't have one).
    33	    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
    34	    steps:
    35	      # Deliberately NOT checked out at github.event.workflow_run.head_sha.
    36	      # workflow_run jobs get real secrets regardless of who triggered the
    37	      # original run — checking out and then executing a PR branch's own
    38	      # version of scripts/*.mjs at that ref would let a modified script on
    39	      # the branch exfiltrate BROWSERSTACK_*/ZEPHYR_*/JIRA_* directly
    40	      # (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25). No ref: means the
    41	      # default branch, which is also the only ref GitHub ever evaluates a
    42	      # workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition from — this job
    43	      # could never have run against a PR branch's version of itself
    44	      # anyway (see .claude/rules/testing.md), so this costs nothing.
    45	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    46	
    47	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    48	        with:
    49	          node-version: '24'
    50	
    51	      # Must use the identical build name the triggering run's
    52	      # e2e-browserstack job computed — not recompute it. This job checks
    53	      # out develop (see above), while e2e-browserstack ran against the
    54	      # PR's own branch; scripts/computeBuildName.mjs's output depends on
    55	      # which @zephyr:-tagged spec files exist in the checkout, so a PR
    56	      # that adds or renames one would get a different computed name here
    57	      # than the triggering run got, and the build lookup below would miss
    58	      # entirely until the PR merges (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly,
    59	      # 2026-08-25, when this only had to account for qa.yml). Downloading
    60	      # the exact string that run persisted removes the drift instead of
    61	      # just documenting it — true for either triggering workflow.
    62	      - name: Download build name artifact from the triggering run
    63	        id: download-build-name
    64	        continue-on-error: true # no artifact means e2e-browserstack didn't run for this run — normal
    65	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
    66	        with:
    67	          name: browserstack-build-name
    68	          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
    69	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
    70	
    71	      # A missing artifact is only safe to shrug off when e2e-browserstack
    72	      # never ran for this triggering run (nothing to sync either way). If
    73	      # it DID run, a real BrowserStack build exists under the Jira-derived
    74	      # name -- silently falling back to the run number would make
    75	      # findBuild() miss it and report "nothing to sync" when there
    76	      # actually is something, hiding a real test failure instead of
    77	      # syncing it (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25, against
    78	      # qa.yml; the same check now covers e2e-browserstack-preview.yml too
    79	      # since both workflows name the job identically).
    80	      - name: Verify build-name availability when e2e-browserstack ran
    81	        if: steps.download-build-name.outcome == 'failure'
    82	        run: |
    83	          CONCLUSION=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}/jobs" \
    84	            --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name == "Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)") | .conclusion')
    85	          if [[ -n "$CONCLUSION" && "$CONCLUSION" != "skipped" ]]; then
    86	            echo "::error::e2e-browserstack ran (conclusion: $CONCLUSION) for this run but its build-name artifact could not be downloaded. Refusing to fall back to the run number, which could silently miss a real BrowserStack build. Investigate the artifact upload step in the triggering workflow."
    87	            exit 1
    88	          fi
    89	          echo "e2e-browserstack did not run (or was skipped) for this run -- the run-number fallback is safe, there's no real build to miss."
    90	        env:
    91	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    92	
    93	      - name: Resolve build name
    94	        id: build-name
    95	        run: |
    96	          if [[ -f browserstack-build-name.txt ]]; then
    97	            NAME=$(cat browserstack-build-name.txt)
    98	          else
    99	            NAME="${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_number }}"
   100	          fi
   101	          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   102	
   103	      - name: Sync BrowserStack results to Zephyr Scale
   104	        run: node scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs
   105	        env:
   106	          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
   107	          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
   108	          # Keep in sync with browserstack.yml's testObservabilityOptions.projectName.
   109	          BROWSERSTACK_PROJECT_NAME: 'Zim Project'
   110	          BROWSERSTACK_BUILD_NAME: 'Sprint-${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}'
   111	          ZEPHYR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_API_KEY }}
   112	          ZEPHYR_API_URL: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_API_URL }}
   113	          JIRA_URL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_URL }}
   114	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
   115	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}

    39	      # the branch exfiltrate BROWSERSTACK_*/ZEPHYR_*/JIRA_* directly

    42	      # workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition from — this job
    43	      # could never have run against a PR branch's version of itself

    59	      # 2026-08-25, when this only had to account for qa.yml). Downloading
    60	      # the exact string that run persisted removes the drift instead of
    61	      # just documenting it — true for either triggering workflow.

    68	          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
    69	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

    72	      # never ran for this triggering run (nothing to sync either way). If
    73	      # it DID run, a real BrowserStack build exists under the Jira-derived
    74	      # name -- silently falling back to the run number would make
    75	      # findBuild() miss it and report "nothing to sync" when there
    76	      # actually is something, hiding a real test failure instead of
    77	      # syncing it (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25, against
    78	      # qa.yml; the same check now covers e2e-browserstack-preview.yml too

Refusing to fall back to the run number, which could silently miss a real BrowserStack build. Investigate the artifact upload step in the triggering workflow."

   107	          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}

   109	          BROWSERSTACK_PROJECT_NAME: 'Zim Project'
   110	          BROWSERSTACK_BUILD_NAME: 'Sprint-${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}'

1	name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)
     2	
     3	# SFCC-751 develop-PR path, split out of qa.yml's e2e-browserstack
     4	# (2026-08-25 cost review). Per-story Zephyr-linked BrowserStack execution
     5	# against a develop-targeted PR's own ephemeral MRT preview
     6	# (deploy-preview.yml), triggered the instant that preview finishes
     7	# building instead of polling for it from an already-running, already-
     8	# billed job. The old design started in parallel with Deploy Preview and
     9	# slept in a loop waiting for it — up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner
    10	# time per push. workflow_run fires exactly once, exactly when Deploy
    11	# Preview completes, with everything this job needs already in the event
    12	# payload or a downloadable artifact — no polling, so no billed wait.
    13	#
    14	# release/** PRs are unaffected — deploy-preview.yml never runs for
    15	# fix/release-* branches, so this workflow never fires for them; they keep
    16	# using qa.yml's e2e-browserstack (full suite, static test tier, no wait).
    17	#
    18	# GitHub only evaluates a workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition
    19	# from the repository's default branch — this file is invisible to Actions
    20	# entirely until merged to develop, and (like zephyr-results-sync.yml) can
    21	# never be dry-run against a real PR pre-merge. See testing.md's note on
    22	# zephyr-results-sync.yml for the same caveat.

    24	  workflow_run:
    25	    workflows: ['Deploy Preview']
    26	    types: [completed]
    27	
    28	permissions:
    29	  contents: read
    30	  actions: read # to download artifacts from the triggering Deploy Preview run and look up its matching QA run
    31	  pull-requests: read # to find the open PR for this branch
    32	
    33	jobs:
    34	  e2e-browserstack:
    35	    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
    36	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    37	    # Only a fully cancelled Deploy Preview run has nothing to fall back to
    38	    # (no hostname artifact could ever exist). Any other conclusion still
    39	    # gets a shot at the static test-tier fallback below — same graceful-
    40	    # degradation the old polling design had.
    41	    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
    42	    timeout-minutes: 25
    43	    environment: test # for vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME (fallback target) and the E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets
    44	    steps:
    45	      # Checked out at the triggering run's own head_sha, not the default
    46	      # branch — this job needs to execute the PR's own e2e specs and
    47	      # scripts/computeBuildName.mjs, not develop's copy of them (unlike
    48	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml, which deliberately checks out develop for
    49	      # a script-trust reason that doesn't apply here — see that
    50	      # workflow's comment). This carries the same secrets-exposure shape
    51	      # qa.yml's old pull_request-triggered e2e-browserstack job already
    52	      # had: real BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_* secrets alongside PR-branch code.
    53	      # Acceptable under this repo's branch model (feature/fix branches
    54	      # only, never a fork — see AGENTS.md > Branch Rules); would need
    55	      # re-review if fork-based PRs are ever introduced.
    56	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    57	        with:
    58	          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
    59	
    60	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    61	        with:
    62	          node-version: '24'
    63	          cache: 'npm'
    64	
    65	      - name: Install dependencies
    66	        run: npm install --include=dev
    67	
    68	      # Single API call, no loop — by the time Deploy Preview has finished
    69	      # (~5-10 min after push), the PR this branch belongs to has existed
    70	      # for the whole run, so there's nothing to wait for here either.
    71	      - name: Find open PR for this branch
    72	        id: pr
    73	        env:
    74	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    75	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
    76	        run: |
    77	          PR_JSON=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open \
    78	            --json number,title,body,baseRefName --jq '.[0] // empty')
    79	          if [[ -z "$PR_JSON" ]]; then
    80	            echo "No open PR found for branch $BRANCH -- nothing to test."
    81	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    82	            exit 0
    83	          fi
    84	          BASE=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.baseRefName')
    85	          if [[ "$BASE" != "develop" ]]; then
    86	            # deploy-preview.yml only triggers on feature/**, fix/** pushes,
    87	            # which per AGENTS.md > Branch Rules always target develop — this
    88	            # is a defensive check, not an expected path.
    89	            echo "PR #$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number') targets $BASE, not develop -- skipping."
    90	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    91	            exit 0
    92	          fi
    93	          echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    94	          echo "number=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    95	          # Title/body go to files, not GITHUB_OUTPUT -- both are
    96	          # attacker-controllable free text and could contain newlines or
    97	          # break a later env: interpolation otherwise.
    98	          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.title' > pr-title.txt
    99	          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.body // ""' > pr-body.txt
   100	
   101	      # Same regex/signal as qa.yml's detect-changes "Detect Jira story
   102	      # keys" step. Duplicated rather than shared across workflows -- small
   103	      # and self-contained, and this workflow has no other dependency on
   104	      # qa.yml's run. No key found -> nothing to scope a per-story
   105	      # BrowserStack/Zephyr run to, so skip (mirrors the old "job doesn't
   106	      # run at all" behaviour, not a fallback-to-full).
   107	      - name: Detect Jira story keys
   108	        id: jira
   109	        if: steps.pr.outputs.skip == 'false'
   110	        env:
   111	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
   112	        run: |
   113	          KEYS=$( { cat pr-title.txt pr-body.txt; printf '%s\n' "$BRANCH"; } \
   114	            | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
   115	          echo "keys=$KEYS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   116	
   117	      # Single-shot lookup of the QA run for this same commit -- no loop.
   118	      # detect-changes (qa.yml) finishes in well under a minute; Deploy
   119	      # Preview takes several minutes minimum, so by the time this job
   120	      # starts, that artifact is essentially guaranteed to already exist.
   121	      # If the lookup or download comes up empty for any reason, fail open
   122	      # (assume e2e-relevant) rather than adding a retry loop to chase an
   123	      # optimisation -- worst case this runs BrowserStack once when
   124	      # detect-changes would have skipped it, not a correctness problem.
   125	      - name: Look up matching QA run
   126	        id: qa-run
   127	        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
   128	        env:
   129	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
   130	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
   131	        run: |
   132	          RUN_ID=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/workflows/qa.yml/runs?head_sha=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty')
   133	          echo "run_id=$RUN_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   134	
   135	      - name: Download e2e-relevance artifact
   136	        id: download-e2e-scope
   137	        if: steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id != ''
   138	        continue-on-error: true
   139	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
   140	        with:
   141	          name: e2e-scope
   142	          run-id: ${{ steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id }}
   143	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
   144	
   145	      - name: Check e2e relevance
   146	        id: relevance
   147	        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
   148	        run: |
   149	          if [[ -f e2e-scope.json ]] && [[ "$(jq -r '.e2e' e2e-scope.json)" == "false" ]]; then
   150	            echo "Nothing e2e-relevant changed on this commit (per qa.yml's detect-changes) -- skipping BrowserStack."
   151	            echo "relevant=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   152	          else
   153	            echo "relevant=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   154	          fi
   155	
   156	      - name: Compute build name
   157	        id: build-name
   158	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   159	        run: |
   160	          PRIMARY_KEY=$(echo "${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}" | awk '{print $1}')
   161	          NAME=$(node scripts/computeBuildName.mjs "$PRIMARY_KEY")
   162	          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   163	        env:
   164	          JIRA_URL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_URL }}
   165	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
   166	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}
   167	
   168	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml downloads this rather than recomputing it
   169	      # -- see that workflow's own comment for the drift reason.
   170	      - name: Persist build name for the Zephyr sync job
   171	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   172	        env:
   173	          BUILD_NAME: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
   174	        run: printf '%s\n' "$BUILD_NAME" > browserstack-build-name.txt
   175	
   176	      - name: Upload build name artifact
   177	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   178	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   179	        with:
   180	          name: browserstack-build-name
   181	          path: browserstack-build-name.txt
   182	          retention-days: 7
   183	
   184	      # Deploy Preview persists this as an artifact on its own run only
   185	      # after a successful build+push (see that workflow's own comment) --
   186	      # a missing artifact here means either that run didn't reach that
   187	      # step, or it failed outright. Either way, fall back to the static
   188	      # test-tier target instead of failing this job, same as the old
   189	      # polling design did.
   190	      - name: Download preview hostname artifact
   191	        id: download-preview-hostname
   192	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   193	        continue-on-error: true
   194	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
   195	        with:
   196	          name: mrt-preview-hostname
   197	          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
   198	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
   199	
   200	      - name: Resolve BrowserStack test target
   201	        id: resolve-target
   202	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   203	        run: |
   204	          if [[ -f preview-hostname.txt ]]; then
   205	            HOSTNAME=$(cat preview-hostname.txt)
   206	            echo "Testing this PR's own MRT preview: https://$HOSTNAME"
   207	            echo "retail_app_home=https://$HOSTNAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   208	          else
   209	            echo "No PR-specific preview available for this run -- falling back to the static test-tier RETAIL_APP_HOME."
   210	            echo "retail_app_home=${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   211	          fi
   212	
   213	      - name: Run Zimmermann e2e on BrowserStack
   214	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   215	        run: |
   216	          GREP=$(echo "$KEYS" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/@/' | paste -sd '|')
   217	          npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep "$GREP"
   218	        env:
   219	          KEYS: ${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}
   220	          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
   221	          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
   222	          SPRINT_NUMBER: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
   223	          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ steps.resolve-target.outputs.retail_app_home }}
   224	          # Sent regardless of which target was resolved above. The `test`
   225	          # tier is access-gated (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-25)
   226	          # -- without this header every request is rejected before the
   227	          # page can load. Whether the PR's own MRT preview target also
   228	          # needs it is unconfirmed, but sending an extra header a target
   229	          # doesn't require is harmless. See BasePage.js's
   230	          # applyExtraHeaders() and testing.md > Access-gated preview URLs.
   231	          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME }}
   232	          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE }}
   233	          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
   234	          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
   235	          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   236	          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   237	          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   238	          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   239	          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}
   240	          SITE_ID: au  # Default — parameterise for multi-region runs

   116	
   117	      # Single-shot lookup of the QA run for this same commit -- no loop.
   118	      # detect-changes (qa.yml) finishes in well under a minute; Deploy

   121	      # If the lookup or download comes up empty for any reason, fail open

   123	      # optimisation -- worst case this runs BrowserStack once when
   124	      # detect-changes would have skipped it, not a correctness problem.
   125	      - name: Look up matching QA run
   126	        id: qa-run

   131	        run: |

   134	
   135	      - name: Download e2e-relevance artifact

   139	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4

   141	          name: e2e-scope
   142	          run-id: ${{ steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id }}
   143	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
   144	
   145	      - name: Check e2e relevance
   146	        id: relevance
   147	        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
   148	        run: |
   149	          if [[ -f e2e-scope.json ]] && [[ "$(jq -r '.e2e' e2e-scope.json)" == "false" ]]; then

   152	          else
   153	            echo "relevant=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   154	          fi
   155	
   156	      - name: Compute build name
   157	        id: build-name
   158	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   159	        run: |

   161	          NAME=$(node scripts/computeBuildName.mjs "$PRIMARY_KEY")
   162	          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   163	        env:

   165	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
   166	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}

   168	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml downloads this rather than recomputing it
   169	      # -- see that workflow's own comment for the drift reason.
   170	      - name: Persist build name for the Zephyr sync job
   171	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   172	        env:
   173	          BUILD_NAME: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
   174	        run: printf '%s\n' "$BUILD_NAME" > browserstack-build-name.txt
   175	
   176	      - name: Upload build name artifact
   177	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   178	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   179	        with:
   180	          name: browserstack-build-name
   181	          path: browserstack-build-name.txt
   182	          retention-days: 7
   183	
   184	      # Deploy Preview persists this as an artifact on its own run only
   185	      # after a successful build+push (see that workflow's own comment) --
   186	      # a missing artifact here means either that run didn't reach that
   187	      # step, or it failed outright. Either way, fall back to the static
   188	      # test-tier target instead of failing this job, same as the old
   189	      # polling design did.
   190	      - name: Download preview hostname artifact
   191	        id: download-preview-hostname
   192	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   193	        continue-on-error: true
   194	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4

   196	          name: mrt-preview-hostname

   198	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

   201	        id: resolve-target

   203	        run: |
   204	          if [[ -f preview-hostname.txt ]]; then

1	name: Deploy Preview
     2	
     3	# Ephemeral per-branch MRT preview environments. On every push to a feature/fix
     4	# branch, creates (or reuses) a dedicated MRT environment, syncs runtime env vars,
     5	# builds, and deploys — giving devs/testers a live URL to review during PR without
     6	# waiting for a merge to develop. Companion teardown workflow: teardown-preview.yml.
     7	#
     8	# Every ephemeral target is prefixed `pr-`, so it can never collide with the fixed
     9	# named environments (dev, dev1, test, sit, stg, uat, production).
    10	
    11	on:
    12	  push:
    13	    branches:
    14	      - 'feature/**'
    15	      - 'fix/**'
    16	      - '!fix/release-*'
    17	      # `*` doesn't match `/` in GitHub Actions branch globs, so the pattern
    18	      # above alone wouldn't exclude a nested fix/release/<version> naming slip
    19	      # — this repo's documented convention is the hyphenated
    20	      # fix/release-{version}-* form, but this guards defensively either way.
    21	      - '!fix/release/**'
    22	
    23	# Keyed on the raw branch name (not the derived slug) — concurrency groups are
    24	# evaluated before any job/step runs, so the key can't depend on a step output.
    25	# cancel-in-progress is deliberately false: a cancelled Actions run does NOT cancel
    26	# an already-submitted MRT-side operation (a POST/PATCH, or an in-flight
    27	# `pwa-kit-dev push`), so a naively-cancelled run's server-side effects could still
    28	# land after its successor starts. Same reasoning deploy-test.yml documents for its
    29	# own cancel-in-progress: false.
    30	concurrency:
    31	  group: mrt-preview-${{ github.ref_name }}
    32	  cancel-in-progress: false
    33	
    34	permissions:
    35	  contents: read
    36	  pull-requests: write
    37	
    38	jobs:
    39	  deploy-preview:
    40	    name: Deploy Preview
    41	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    42	    # Deliberately NOT bound to a GitHub Environment. It used to declare
    43	    # `environment: dev`, which made GitHub log a real Deployment tagged
    44	    # "dev" on every single push to a feature/fix branch -- every PR showed
    45	    # a misleading "Deployed to dev" even though the actual target is
    46	    # always an isolated pr-<slug> MRT preview, never the shared dev tier
    47	    # (confirmed against real Deployment records, 2026-08-25). The binding
    48	    # wasn't doing anything functional either: MRT_USER/MRT_API_KEY below
    49	    # are already repo-level secrets, the dev-tier Variables this job
    50	    # actually needs are fetched explicitly via the GitHub API further down
    51	    # (SOURCE_ENV: dev, using GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN) rather than the native
    52	    # environment: binding, and `dev` carries no protection rules to lose.
    53	    # 12 min target-wait deadline + headroom for npm install/build/push — a
    54	    # tighter timeout could cancel the job mid-wait, and a cancelled Actions run
    55	    # does not cancel an already-submitted MRT-side operation (see the
    56	    # concurrency note above), so the timeout needs real margin over the wait
    57	    # budget, not just the wait budget itself.
    58	    timeout-minutes: 35
    59	    env:
    60	      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
    61	      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
    62	      MRT_PROJECT: zimmermann
    63	    steps:
    64	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    65	
    66	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    67	        with:
    68	          node-version: '24'
    69	          cache: 'npm'
    70	
    71	      - name: Install dependencies
    72	        run: npm install --include=dev
    73	
    74	      - name: Compute MRT preview slug
    75	        id: slug
    76	        env:
    77	          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
    78	        run: |
    79	          SLUG=$(node scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs "$BRANCH_NAME")
    80	          echo "slug=$SLUG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    81	
    82	      - name: Read desired proxy config from config/dev.js
    83	        id: proxy
    84	        run: |
    85	          PROXY_JSON=$(node -e "
    86	            const cfgs = require('./config/dev.js')?.ssrParameters?.proxyConfigs
    87	            if (!Array.isArray(cfgs) || cfgs.length === 0) {
    88	              console.error('config/dev.js has no ssrParameters.proxyConfigs')
    89	              process.exit(1)
    90	            }
    91	            console.log(JSON.stringify(cfgs))
    92	          ")
    93	          echo "json=$PROXY_JSON" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    94	
    95	      # Region and proxy config are NOT derived from the bundle push — confirmed
    96	      # live this session: two successful `pwa-kit-dev push` calls left
    97	      # ssr_proxy_configs null on a freshly created target, and region defaults to
    98	      # us-east-2 unless set explicitly. Both must be set here, explicitly, and
    99	      # self-healed on every run in case a target was ever created out-of-band
   100	      # (e.g. by hand through the MRT console) with the wrong values.
   101	      - name: Ensure MRT target exists with correct region/proxy config
   102	        id: ensure
   103	        env:
   104	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
   105	          PROXY_JSON: ${{ steps.proxy.outputs.json }}
   106	        run: |
   107	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
   108	          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
   109	
   110	          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
   111	          USER, API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_USER'], os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
   112	          DESIRED_PROXY = json.loads(os.environ['PROXY_JSON'])
   113	          DESIRED_REGION = 'ap-southeast-2'
   114	
   115	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
   116	          headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {token}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
   117	          base = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/'
   118	
   119	          def get_target():
   120	              req = urllib.request.Request(base + f'target/{SLUG}/', headers=headers)
   121	              for attempt in range(3):
   122	                  try:
   123	                      return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
   124	                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
   125	                      if e.code == 404:
   126	                          return None
   127	                      if attempt < 2 and (e.code == 429 or e.code >= 500):
   128	                          print(f'Transient HTTP {e.code} on target lookup — backing off 30s')
   129	                          time.sleep(30)
   130	                          continue
   131	                      raise
   132	                  except urllib.error.URLError as e:
   133	                      if attempt < 2:
   134	                          print(f'Connection error on target lookup ({e.reason}) — backing off 30s')
   135	                          time.sleep(30)
   136	                          continue
   137	                      raise
   138	
   139	          def proxy_matches(existing_proxy):
   140	              if not existing_proxy:
   141	                  return False
   142	              # Compare the full config per entry, not just path/host — a field
   143	              # this repo doesn't use today drifting silently would otherwise
   144	              # never trigger the self-heal PATCH below.
   145	              norm = lambda cfgs: sorted(json.dumps(c, sort_keys=True) for c in cfgs)
   146	              return norm(existing_proxy) == norm(DESIRED_PROXY)
   147	
   148	          existing = get_target()
   149	          if existing is None:
   150	              print(f'No existing target for {SLUG} — creating in {DESIRED_REGION}.')
   151	              payload = {
   152	                  'name': SLUG,
   153	                  'ssr_region': DESIRED_REGION,
   154	                  'ssr_proxy_configs': DESIRED_PROXY,
   155	              }
   156	              req = urllib.request.Request(
   157	                  base + 'target/', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method='POST', headers=headers
   158	              )
   159	              try:
   160	                  resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
   161	                  print(f'Create requested: {resp.status}')
   162	              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
   163	                  print(f'Create failed {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
   164	                  sys.exit(1)
   165	          else:
   166	              print(f'Target {SLUG} already exists (state={existing.get("state")}) — reusing.')
   167	              needs_patch = (
   168	                  existing.get('ssr_region') != DESIRED_REGION
   169	                  or not proxy_matches(existing.get('ssr_proxy_configs'))
   170	              )
   171	              if needs_patch:
   172	                  print(f'Target {SLUG} has drifted region/proxy config — self-healing.')
   173	                  payload = {'ssr_region': DESIRED_REGION, 'ssr_proxy_configs': DESIRED_PROXY}
   174	                  req = urllib.request.Request(
   175	                      base + f'target/{SLUG}/', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method='PATCH', headers=headers
   176	                  )
   177	                  try:
   178	                      urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
   179	                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
   180	                      print(f'Region/proxy patch failed {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
   181	                      sys.exit(1)
   182	                  # The PATCH alone updates target config but not the already-running
   183	                  # Lambda — confirmed live, the relocation only takes effect after the
   184	                  # next `pwa-kit-dev push`, which always runs later in this job.
   185	          PYEOF
   186	
   187	      - name: Wait for target to reach ACTIVE
   188	        id: wait
   189	        env:
   190	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
   191	        run: |
   192	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
   193	          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
   194	
   195	          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
   196	          USER, API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_USER'], os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
   197	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
   198	          headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {token}'}
   199	          url = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{SLUG}/'
   200	
   201	          # Fresh create ~5 min, region-relocation redeploy ~2 min, per validated
   202	          # session data — poll generously but bounded so a stuck target fails loudly.
   203	          deadline, poll_every = time.time() + 12 * 60, 20
   204	          while True:
   205	              req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
   206	              try:
   207	                  body = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
   208	              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
   209	                  if e.code == 429:
   210	                      if time.time() > deadline:
   211	                          print('Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (persistently rate limited)', file=sys.stderr)
   212	                          sys.exit(1)
   213	                      try:
   214	                          backoff = max(1, min(60, int(e.headers.get('Retry-After', 30))))
   215	                      except (TypeError, ValueError):
   216	                          backoff = 30
   217	                      print(f'Rate limited — backing off {backoff}s')
   218	                      time.sleep(backoff)
   219	                      continue
   220	                  # The create request is asynchronous — a freshly-created target
   221	                  # can briefly 404 (not yet visible) or 5xx before settling, not
   222	                  # just while waiting on state transitions. Retry those like any
   223	                  # other not-yet-ready signal instead of failing the job outright.
   224	                  if e.code == 404 or e.code >= 500:
   225	                      print(f'Transient HTTP {e.code} — target not visible yet, retrying')
   226	                      if time.time() > deadline:
   227	                          print(f'Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (last error={e.code})', file=sys.stderr)
   228	                          sys.exit(1)
   229	                      time.sleep(poll_every)
   230	                      continue
   231	                  raise
   232	              except urllib.error.URLError as e:
   233	                  print(f'Connection error ({e.reason}) — retrying')
   234	                  if time.time() > deadline:
   235	                      print('Timed out waiting for ACTIVE', file=sys.stderr)
   236	                      sys.exit(1)
   237	                  time.sleep(poll_every)
   238	                  continue
   239	              state = body.get('state')
   240	              print(f'target {SLUG} state={state}')
   241	              if state == 'ACTIVE':
   242	                  # Read the real hostname from the API rather than assuming a
   243	                  # fixed host suffix — that suffix is MRT-account-specific and
   244	                  # could change; a hardcoded guess would silently publish a dead
   245	                  # URL in the PR comment if it ever did.
   246	                  hostname = body.get('ssr_external_hostname')
   247	                  if not hostname:
   248	                      print('Target is ACTIVE but ssr_external_hostname is empty', file=sys.stderr)
   249	                      sys.exit(1)
   250	                  with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
   251	                      out.write(f'hostname={hostname}\n')
   252	                  break
   253	              if state and state.endswith('_FAILED'):
   254	                  print(f'Target entered failed state: {state}', file=sys.stderr)
   255	                  sys.exit(1)
   256	              if time.time() > deadline:
   257	                  print(f'Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (last state={state})', file=sys.stderr)
   258	                  sys.exit(1)
   259	              time.sleep(poll_every)
   260	          PYEOF
   261	
   262	      # Steps below lift .github/workflows/sync-env-vars-to-mrt.yml's env-var-sync
   263	      # logic near-verbatim. The one structural change: source (which GitHub
   264	      # Environment to read from) and destination (which MRT target to PATCH) are
   265	      # no longer the same value — source is always `dev`+`shared` regardless of
   266	      # branch, since there's no per-branch GitHub Environment; destination is the
   267	      # computed slug.
   268	      - name: Parse syncable keys from .env.sample
   269	        id: parse
   270	        run: |
   271	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
   272	          import re, os, json
   273	
   274	          # Only keys explicitly tagged `# mrt:true` in .env.sample are synced.
   275	          keys = []
   276	          pending_mrt = False
   277	          with open('.env.sample') as f:
   278	              for line in f:
   279	                  line = line.rstrip('\n')
   280	                  if re.match(r'^#\s*mrt:true', line):
   281	                      pending_mrt = True
   282	                      continue
   283	                  stripped = line.strip()
   284	                  if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
   285	                      if not stripped:
   286	                          pending_mrt = False
   287	                      continue
   288	                  eq = stripped.find('=')
   289	                  if eq == -1:
   290	                      pending_mrt = False
   291	                      continue
   292	                  key = stripped[:eq].strip()
   293	                  if pending_mrt:
   294	                      keys.append(key)
   295	                  pending_mrt = False
   296	
   297	          print(f'Parsed {len(keys)} MRT-tagged keys from .env.sample')
   298	          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
   299	              out.write(f'keys={json.dumps(keys)}\n')
   300	          PYEOF
   301	
   302	      - name: Fetch GitHub Environment variables (dev + shared)
   303	        id: gh_vars
   304	        env:
   305	          # Always dev — ephemeral preview branches have no GitHub Environment of
   306	          # their own to source from.
   307	          SOURCE_ENV: dev
   308	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
   309	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN }}
   310	        run: |
   311	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
   312	          import json, os, subprocess, sys
   313	
   314	          SOURCE_ENV = os.environ['SOURCE_ENV']
   315	          REPO = os.environ['REPO']
   316	
   317	          def fetch_env(env_name):
   318	              """Fetch all variables from a GitHub Environment. Returns dict of name→value."""
   319	              import urllib.parse
   320	              safe_name = urllib.parse.quote(env_name, safe='')
   321	              result = subprocess.run(
   322	                  ['gh', 'api', f'/repos/{REPO}/environments/{safe_name}/variables',
   323	                   '--paginate', '--jq', '.variables[] | {(.name): .value}'],
   324	                  capture_output=True, text=True
   325	              )
   326	              if result.returncode != 0:
   327	                  print(f'GitHub API error fetching {env_name}: {result.stderr}', file=sys.stderr)
   328	                  sys.exit(1)
   329	              out = {}
   330	              for line in result.stdout.strip().splitlines():
   331	                  if line:
   332	                      out.update(json.loads(line))
   333	              return out
   334	
   335	          shared_vars = fetch_env('shared')
   336	          target_vars = fetch_env(SOURCE_ENV)
   337	          all_vars = dict(shared_vars)
   338	          for name, value in target_vars.items():
   339	              if value or name not in all_vars:
   340	                  all_vars[name] = value
   341	
   342	          print(f'Found {len(shared_vars)} variables in GitHub Environment: shared')
   343	          print(f'Found {len(target_vars)} variables in GitHub Environment: {SOURCE_ENV}')
   344	          print(f'Merged total (target overrides shared): {len(all_vars)}')
   345	
   346	          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
   347	              out.write(f'vars={json.dumps(all_vars)}\n')
   348	          PYEOF
   349	
   350	      - name: Sync env vars to the preview target
   351	        env:
   352	          MRT_TARGET_SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
   353	          SYNC_KEYS: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.keys }}
   354	          GH_VARS: ${{ steps.gh_vars.outputs.vars }}
   355	        run: |
   356	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
   357	          import base64, json, os, sys, urllib.request, urllib.error
   358	
   359	          TARGET  = os.environ['MRT_TARGET_SLUG']
   360	          PROJECT = os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
   361	          USER    = os.environ['MRT_USER']
   362	          API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
   363	
   364	          syncable_keys = json.loads(os.environ['SYNC_KEYS'])
   365	          gh_vars       = json.loads(os.environ['GH_VARS'])
   366	
   367	          payload = {}
   368	          skipped_empty = []
   369	          skipped_missing = []
   370	          for key in syncable_keys:
   371	              if key in gh_vars:
   372	                  val = gh_vars[key]
   373	                  if val:
   374	                      payload[key] = {'value': val}
   375	                  else:
   376	                      skipped_empty.append(key)
   377	              else:
   378	                  skipped_missing.append(key)
   379	
   380	          print(f'Keys to sync:    {len(payload)}')
   381	          print(f'Skipped (empty): {len(skipped_empty)}')
   382	          print(f'Skipped (not in GitHub Environment): {len(skipped_missing)}')
   383	
   384	          if not payload:
   385	              print('Nothing to sync.')
   386	              sys.exit(0)
   387	
   388	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
   389	          url   = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{TARGET}/env-var/'
   390	          req   = urllib.request.Request(
   391	              url,
   392	              data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
   393	              method='PATCH',
   394	              headers={
   395	                  'Authorization': f'Basic {token}',
   396	                  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
   397	              },
   398	          )
   399	          try:
   400	              resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
   401	              print(f'\nMRT response: {resp.status} {resp.reason}')
   402	              print(f'Synced {len(payload)} env vars to MRT target: {TARGET}')
   403	          except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
   404	              print(f'MRT API error {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
   405	              sys.exit(1)
   406	          except urllib.error.URLError as e:
   407	              print(f'MRT API connection error: {e.reason}', file=sys.stderr)
   408	              sys.exit(1)
   409	          PYEOF
   410	
   411	      # Must run after env vars are synced, not before — a target with no env
   412	      # vars 500s on every request (confirmed live).
   413	      - name: Build and push to preview target
   414	        env:
   415	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
   416	        run: |
   417	          npm run build
   418	          npx pwa-kit-dev push -t "$SLUG" -w
   419	
   420	      # Deliberately placed after the push above, not right after the "wait
   421	      # for ACTIVE" step that first produced steps.wait.outputs.hostname --
   422	      # the target existing and being ACTIVE only means the MRT
   423	      # infrastructure is ready, not that this PR's own code is live there
   424	      # yet. e2e-browserstack (qa.yml) downloads this artifact and points
   425	      # BrowserStack at the resulting URL instead of the static test-tier
   426	      # RETAIL_APP_HOME, so it actually tests this PR's own changes rather
   427	      # than whatever unrelated build happens to be live on test tier
   428	      # (test is a deliberate, tag-promoted environment with no guaranteed
   429	      # relationship to any given PR -- confirmed with the developer,
   430	      # 2026-08-25). Short retention: only needed within this PR's own CI
   431	      # cycle, never referenced again after.
   432	      - name: Persist preview hostname for e2e-browserstack
   433	        env:
   434	          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
   435	        run: printf '%s\n' "$PREVIEW_HOSTNAME" > preview-hostname.txt
   436	
   437	      - name: Upload preview hostname artifact
   438	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   439	        with:
   440	          name: mrt-preview-hostname
   441	          path: preview-hostname.txt
   442	          retention-days: 1
   443	
   444	      - name: Find open PR for this branch
   445	        id: pr
   446	        env:
   447	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
   448	          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
   449	        run: |
   450	          NUMBER=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
   451	          echo "number=$NUMBER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   452	
   453	      # Upserts on an exact HTML-comment marker (not a text substring) so a
   454	      # coincidental match in someone else's comment can't be mistaken for ours,
   455	      # and so redeploys update the same comment instead of spamming the thread —
   456	      # the URL is deterministic from the slug and never changes between pushes.
   457	      # Pattern mirrors protected-file-guard.yml's Tier 2 warning comment.
   458	      - name: Post or update preview URL comment
   459	        if: steps.pr.outputs.number != ''
   460	        uses: actions/github-script@v7
   461	        env:
   462	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.number }}
   463	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
   464	          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
   465	        with:
   466	          script: |
   467	            const prNumber = Number(process.env.PR_NUMBER)
   468	            const marker = `<!-- mrt-preview:${process.env.SLUG} -->`
   469	            const previewUrl = `https://${process.env.PREVIEW_HOSTNAME}`
   470	            const body = `${marker}\n## 🚀 MRT Preview Environment\n\n**Live preview:** ${previewUrl}\n\nTarget: \`${process.env.SLUG}\` · Updated: ${new Date().toISOString()}\n\n_Auto-updated on every push to this branch. Torn down when this PR closes or the branch is deleted._`
   471	
   472	            // Paginated — listComments only returns the first page (30) by
   473	            // default, which would miss the marker on a busy PR and start
   474	            // duplicating comments instead of updating in place. c.body is
   475	            // optional in the REST payload, so guard against null too.
   476	            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments, {
   477	              owner: context.repo.owner,
   478	              repo: context.repo.repo,
   479	              issue_number: prNumber,
   480	              per_page: 100,
   481	            })
   482	            const existing = comments.find(
   483	              (c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(marker) && c.user?.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
   484	            )
   485	            if (existing) {
   486	              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
   487	                owner: context.repo.owner,
   488	                repo: context.repo.repo,
   489	                comment_id: existing.id,
   490	                body,
   491	              })
   492	            } else {
   493	              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
   494	                owner: context.repo.owner,
   495	                repo: context.repo.repo,
   496	                issue_number: prNumber,
   497	                body,
   498	              })
   499	            }
